tasks.text: Fill every clean container, tub, and pot with water while taps still work
tasks.detail: Water pressure often fails in the first days. Bathtubs, pots, bottles, and jugs all count.

tasks.text: Shut off the water heater's power/gas and note it holds 30–80 gallons of drinkable water
tasks.detail: Drain from the valve at the bottom into a clean container. Let sediment settle.

tasks.text: Check water days-left on the Supplies screen
tasks.detail: Each person needs about 1 gallon (3.8 L) a day; double it in heat.

tasks.text: Treat any water that isn't from sealed bottles
tasks.detail: Boil 1 minute (3 above 6,500 ft) or use bleach. See Calculators.

tasks.text: Set out clean containers or tarps to catch rain
tasks.detail: Treat rainwater before drinking.

tasks.text: Find and pin a backup water source on the map
tasks.detail: Creek, pond, spring, or a neighbor's well. Pin it so everyone knows.

tasks.text: Clean or backflush your water filter
tasks.detail: A clogged filter wastes effort and can let germs through.

tasks.text: Eat food from the fridge first, then the freezer, then pantry
tasks.detail: Fridge food is safe about 4 hours without power; a full freezer about 48. See Calculators.

tasks.text: Count your food and enter it in Supplies with calories
tasks.detail: Calories are on the label: multiply calories per serving by servings.

tasks.text: Plan today's meals from what spoils soonest
Cook outdoors only (grill, camp stove)
tasks.detail: Never use a grill, camp stove, or generator indoors, in a garage, or near windows: carbon monoxide kills.

tasks.text: Tend a garden or sprouts if you can
tasks.detail: Even sprouted beans or lentils add fresh food in a week.

tasks.text: Preserve extra food (drying, salting, canning)
tasks.detail: See the USDA canning guide in Field manuals before canning low-acid foods.

tasks.text: Feed and water the pets
tasks.detail: Pets need water too; it's included in your water estimate.

tasks.text: Give medications on schedule and update counts
tasks.detail: Check the medication runway in Supplies.

tasks.text: Gather first-aid supplies into one kit everyone knows
tasks.detail: Tourniquet, gauze, tape, gloves, pain relievers, any prescriptions.

tasks.text: Wash hands with soap before food and after the toilet
tasks.detail: Most outage illnesses spread from hands to food.

tasks.text: Set up a bucket toilet if water stops
tasks.detail: Line a bucket with two bags; add sawdust, soil, or cat litter after each use. Bury or bag waste away from water.

tasks.text: Check everyone for injuries, rashes, fever, or low mood
Hot day? Rest in the shade midday and drink before you're thirsty
Cold? Gather everyone into one small room and dress in layers
tasks.detail: Never use outdoor heaters, grills, or generators indoors.

tasks.text: Check formula, diapers, and the baby's wet diapers (6+ a day)
Keep a sleep schedule; take turns resting
Check that generators and grills are outside, 20+ ft from doors and windows
tasks.detail: Carbon monoxide has no smell. Headache, dizziness, and nausea in several people means get to fresh air now.

tasks.text: Lock doors and windows at dusk; agree who checks
Keep flashlights within reach; avoid candles
tasks.detail: Candles cause many outage house fires.

tasks.text: Locate fire extinguishers and agree on a fire escape plan
tasks.detail: Two ways out of every room; a meeting spot outside.

tasks.text: Keep a low profile: don't advertise supplies or lights at night
Check on trusted neighbors; agree on a signal for help
tasks.detail: A neighborhood watch rota covers more ground with less sleep lost.

tasks.text: Pin your rally points and safe places on the map
tasks.detail: Home, a backup meeting place, nearest clinic, water source.

tasks.text: Fill in the family plan (contacts, rally points) and print the card
tasks.detail: Toolkit → Print cards. Paper works when phones die.

tasks.text: Listen for news on AM/NOAA weather radio at your scheduled times
tasks.detail: See Radio for frequencies and your listening schedule.

tasks.text: Family check-in at an agreed time
tasks.detail: Use Family mesh between phones, or radios.

tasks.text: Charge phones and radios while the sun is strongest
tasks.detail: See Power for today's charging plan.

tasks.text: Keep phones in airplane mode unless you're using them
tasks.detail: With no cell signal, phones waste battery searching for towers.

tasks.text: Write down any news you hear in the radio log
tasks.detail: Note time, station, and what was said.

tasks.text: Keep a simple routine: wake, meals, chores, bedtime
Spend time together: talk about the day and what went well
Give kids a job and some play time
tasks.detail: Jobs help children feel useful and safe.

tasks.text: Read, play a game, or learn something from the Library
Get some daylight and movement
Write a short note about today
tasks.detail: Notes → new note. Helps memory and morale.
